title: Symmetry-Dependent Polarity Reversal of Bulk Spin-Orbit Torque in Single-Layer MnCoGa
authors: Rongkun Han, Mingsong Zhang, Dahai Wei, Yuan Lu, Wenxu Zhang, Jianhua Zhao
abstract: Controlling the magnitude and polarity of spin-orbit torque (SOT) is essential for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices. Here, we realize bulk spin-orbit torque (SOT) in a single-layer Mn1.6Co1.4Ga (MCG) Heusler alloy and achieve lattice strain-controlled reversal of SOT polarity. SOT-driven magnetization switching is achieved over a thickness range of 3-20 nm, with the switching polarity reversed between the strongly strained ultrathin regime and thicker films. First-principles calculations reveal a sizable intrinsic spin Hall conductivity (SHC) in MCG originating from its topological band structure, which is enhanced by the tetragonal distortion without changing sign. Together with the thickness-dependent structural evolution, we demonstrate that the reversal of SOT polarity does not originate from a sign change of the SHC, but rather from lattice distortion induced symmetry breaking that modifies the conversion of spin current into a net bulk SOT, thereby controlling its polarity. These results establish strain-controlled structural symmetry as an additional degree of freedom for tuning bulk SOT in magnetic single layers.
summary: This work demonstrates that the polarity of the spin-orbit torque in a magnetic single layer can be precisely controlled by engineering the structural symmetry through lattice strain. By analyzing the MnCoGa alloy, the authors show that the reversal of SOT polarity is due to changes in the lattice distortion gradient, providing a powerful, structure-based degree of freedom for spintronic device design.
main_problem: The core problem is controlling the magnitude and polarity of the spin-orbit torque (SOT) for efficient magnetization manipulation in spintronic devices.
main_result: The SOT polarity can be reversed by controlling the lattice strain and structural symmetry of the single-layer magnetic material, rather than relying solely on the sign change of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity.
method: The study combines first-principles calculations (DFT) to model intrinsic spin Hall conductivity with experimental measurements (Varying thickness, transport measurements) to observe SOT switching behavior.
model_or_system: The system is a single-layer Mn1.6Co1.4Ga (MCG) Heusler alloy grown on a substrate, whose structural evolution (lattice strain/distortion) is key to the observed physical properties.
key_observables: Damping-like torque efficiency ($\chi_{DL}$), magnetization switching polarity, and the lattice constant/distortion gradient as a function of film thickness.
important_parameters: Film thickness (3-20 nm), lattice strain/tetragonal distortion, and the structural symmetry breaking mechanism.
main_assumptions: The SOT is governed by a symmetry-dependent conversion of spin current into torque, and the intrinsic SHC alone is insufficient to predict the polarity reversal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate XRD results showing c-axis change with thickness, magnetization switching curves showing polarity reversal, and theoretical plots linking SHC and torque coefficients to lattice distortion.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for SOT control, presents the material system and measurement techniques, theoretically calculates SHC dependence on distortion, and finally links the observed thickness-dependent SOT polarity reversal to the sign change in the lattice distortion gradient.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the concept of using structural symmetry breaking (a geometric/topological constraint) to control a macroscopic transport property (SOT polarity) is analogous to engineering boundary conditions or symmetries in quantum simulation setups.
